2027-05-10.title: Monday of the Seventh Week of Easter
readings: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?
Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth (or: Alleluia)
Take courage; I have conquered the world
2027-05-10.alt: Easter weekday. The paschal candle burns beside the ambo; the Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli (Queen of Heaven) replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white. Optional memorial of St John of Avila, priest and doctor of the Church (in the General Roman Calendar since 2021). The days between the Ascension and Pentecost: the novena to the Holy Spirit continues.
2027-05-10.verse: I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!
theo: Paul arrives in Ephesus and meets “some disciples,” about twelve of them. Something about them makes him ask a direct question: “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” Their answer is startling: “No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.” They had been baptized “into John's baptism,” the baptism of repentance that prepared the way for the Messiah. They were sincere; they had begun the journey; but they had stopped at the door. Paul explains gently: “John baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one who was to come after him, that is, in Jesus.” They are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and “when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.” It is a small Pentecost in Ephesus, like the one in Samaria (Acts 8:14–17) and in the house of Cornelius (Acts 10:44–48). The Church has always seen here the two moments of Christian initiation: Baptism, and the laying on of hands that we call Confirmation.

The question Paul asked those twelve is worth asking ourselves in this week before Pentecost. Many of us were baptized as babies and confirmed as children. We have heard that there is a Holy Spirit; we say it every Sunday in the Creed. But do we live as people who have received him? Do we pray to him, listen to him, expect anything of him? Paul spent three months in the synagogue, “arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.” The Spirit makes the Church speak. The Psalm sings of the God who rises up and scatters his enemies, “Father of orphans and protector of widows,” who “gives the desolate a home to live in”: that is what the Spirit does in the Church, making a home for the lonely and a family for the orphaned.

In the Gospel the disciples, at the end of the Last Supper, think at last that they understand: “Yes, now you are speaking plainly … by this we believe that you came from God.” Jesus answers with a sad, loving realism: “Do you now believe? The hour is coming, indeed it has come, when you will be scattered, each one to his home, and you will leave me alone.” Within hours they would run away. Yet Jesus is not bitter: “I am not alone because the Father is with me.” And his last words before the great prayer of John 17 are words of courage: “In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!” He says this before the cross, as if the victory were already won, because it is. St John of Avila, whom the Church remembers today, knew persecution from within the Church itself: as a young priest he was denounced to the Inquisition and spent about a year in prison. There, he said, he learned more of the mystery of Christ than in all his studies. He came out without bitterness, and became the great preacher of Andalusia and a guide of saints.
conn: Paul's base for more than two years (Acts 19:10), from which the Gospel spread through the province of Asia. Tradition also links Ephesus with St John the Apostle and with the Blessed Virgin Mary.
Luke uses the word for believers, but they knew only John's baptism, like Apollos in Saturday's reading. Disciples of John the Baptist were found well beyond Palestine.

A baptism of repentance, preparing for the Messiah (Luke 3:3, 16). Christian Baptism is baptism “in the name of the Lord Jesus,” into his death and Resurrection, with the gift of the Spirit (Romans 6:3–4).

A gesture of blessing and of handing on the Spirit (Acts 8:17; 1 Timothy 4:14; Hebrews 6:2). In the Latin Church it is completed in Confirmation by the anointing with chrism and the words: Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.
Perhaps a quiet echo of the Twelve: a new beginning of the Church in Ephesus.
An ancient processional hymn of God marching from Sinai to his sanctuary. Verse 18, “You ascended the high mount, leading captives,” is quoted in Ephesians 4:8 of Christ's Ascension.
The Greek nenikēka is in the perfect tense: a victory already won and still in force. 1 John 5:4 takes it up: “this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”

A Spanish secular priest, the “Apostle of Andalusia.” He wrote Audi, filia on the spiritual life, guided St John of God, St Francis Borgia and others, and was consulted by St Teresa of Avila. Canonized in 1970, declared a Doctor of the Church by Benedict XVI in 2012; patron of the secular clergy of Spain.
altar: The Spirit who came on the twelve at Ephesus is called down at every Mass. In the epiclesis the priest stretches out his hands over the bread and wine, as Paul laid his hands on the disciples, and asks the Father to send the Holy Spirit so that they may become the Body and Blood of Christ.

St John of Avila taught priests to celebrate Mass as men in love with the Eucharist; he said (in substance) that the priest should be so united to Christ in the sacrifice that his whole life becomes an offering.
outline: Ask: if someone asked you, have you received the Holy Spirit? what would you answer?
Point 1 · We have not even heard
Point 2 · Paul laid his hands on them
Baptism, Confirmation, and a little Pentecost.
The Lord who has conquered the world.
A circle of new believers in Ephesus, Paul's hands on their heads, and their faces bright with prayer.
“Take courage; I have conquered the world!”
live: Find out the date of your Confirmation, or ask your parents. Thank God for it today, and pray the prayer: Come, Holy Spirit.
Pray to the Spirit by name
Each day until Pentecost, ask the Holy Spirit for one of his seven gifts: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord.
Face one difficulty today that you have been avoiding, saying: Jesus, you have conquered the world; give me courage.
fathers: St Cyril of Jerusalem (Mystagogical Catecheses, in substance)

Do not think that the holy chrism is plain ointment. As the bread of the Eucharist after the invocation of the Holy Spirit is no longer simple bread, so this holy oil after the invocation is the gift of Christ and of the Holy Spirit.
St Ambrose (On the Mysteries, in substance)

Remember that you have received the spiritual seal, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, the Spirit of holy fear. Keep what you have received.
The Lord says: I have conquered the world. Rejoice, then, for if he conquered, we too conquer in him. He did not say: you will not be troubled, but: take courage.
magis: From that time on the apostles, in fulfilment of Christ's will, imparted to the newly baptized by the laying on of hands the gift of the Spirit that completes the grace of Baptism (Acts 8:15–17; 19:5–6).

Confirmation brings an increase and deepening of baptismal grace: it unites us more firmly to Christ, increases the gifts of the Holy Spirit in us, and gives us strength to spread and defend the faith.
By Confirmation the faithful are more perfectly bound to the Church and endowed with the special strength of the Holy Spirit, so that they are more strictly obliged to spread and defend the faith.
Fortitude ensures firmness in difficulties and constancy in the pursuit of the good: “In the world you have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.”
Benedict XVI, Apostolic Letter on St John of Avila (7 October 2012)
A master of evangelizers and of priests, whose doctrine of the love of God and of the Eucharist remains a light for the new evangelization.
saints: Born in Almodóvar del Campo, Spain, he studied at Salamanca and Alcalá, gave away his inheritance to the poor, and longed to be a missionary in Mexico, but was kept in Andalusia, where he preached for some forty years. He founded schools and colleges, renewed the clergy, and died at Montilla on 10 May 1569.

A Belgian priest of the Congregation of the Sacred Hearts who served the people with leprosy on Molokai in Hawaii, caught the disease himself and died in 1889. He was canonized in 2009; in the United States he is remembered on 10 May.
2027-05-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you told your disciples: take courage, I have conquered the world. We confess that we too are often afraid, and that we know the Holy Spirit only a little. Send him upon us as he came on the disciples at Ephesus when Paul laid his hands on them. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism and Confirmation; give us his gifts of wisdom and fortitude; and make us witnesses who speak boldly of the kingdom of God. Through the prayers of St John of Avila, give your Church holy priests who love the Eucharist and preach your Word with fire. In you may we have peace. You live and reign for ever and ever. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: In Ephesus Paul found disciples who had not even heard of the Holy Spirit; he baptized them in the name of Jesus and laid his hands on them, and the Spirit came upon them.
Paul spoke boldly in the synagogue for three months about the kingdom of God.
Jesus warned that the disciples would scatter, but said: take courage; I have conquered the world.
2027-05-10.action: Find out the date of your Confirmation and thank God for it today with the prayer “Come, Holy Spirit.”
2027-05-10.question: Do I live as someone who has received the Holy Spirit, or as one who has hardly heard of him?
catechism: The laying on of hands in Acts.
kidsaint: Father Damien was a priest from Belgium who went to an island in Hawaii where people with leprosy had been sent away from their families. Nobody wanted to go there. He built houses, a church and a school, dressed their wounds and played with the children. In the end he caught leprosy too, and he said: now I am one of you. Lesson: the Holy Spirit gives us courage to love people that others are afraid of.
2027-05-10.special: Easter weekday; St John of Avila (optional memorial). Novena to the Holy Spirit. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: The sacrament that completes baptismal grace by the special outpouring of the Holy Spirit, given by the anointing with chrism on the forehead with the laying on of the hand and the words “Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.” In the Latin Church it is usually conferred by the bishop.

family.explain: Paul met some believers in Ephesus and asked them: did you receive the Holy Spirit? They said: we have never even heard of the Holy Spirit! So Paul baptized them in Jesus' name, put his hands on their heads and prayed, and the Holy Spirit came on them. We received the Holy Spirit in Baptism and Confirmation. He lives in us and helps us to be brave and good.
family.intention: We pray for children and young people preparing for Confirmation, and for all who are being persecuted for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we need courage in our family?” Pray together for one another: Holy Spirit, make us brave.

illus: A Confirmation class in a parish in Ernakulam was asked by the catechist to write one sentence about the Holy Spirit. Most wrote what they had learned: the third Person of the Holy Trinity. One boy wrote: I do not know who he is. The catechist did not scold him. She asked the whole class to pray for one minute every evening, Come, Holy Spirit, and to note anything that happened. Three weeks later the same boy wrote: I apologized to my brother, and I did not want to. I think that was him.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers? (Acts 19:2). How would I answer Paul's question today?
When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them (Acts 19:6). What do I remember of my Confirmation, and how has it borne fruit?
Take courage; I have conquered the world! (John 16:33). Where do I need the courage of Christ this week?
pm.resp: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.
interc: For all who will receive Confirmation this year, that they may be filled with the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
For Christians who are persecuted or discriminated against because of their faith, that they may take courage in Christ.
For priests, that through the prayers of St John of Avila they may be holy, learned and full of love for the Eucharist.
For orphans, widows and the lonely, that the Church may be a home for them.
For our group, that in these days before Pentecost we may come to know the Holy Spirit more deeply.
pm.close: Father, your Son has conquered the world. Pour out on us the Spirit of courage and peace, so that we may witness to him without fear. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, imagine Paul walking into Ephesus and meeting twelve people who say they are believers. He looks at them and asks a simple question: did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers? And they answer: no, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit (Acts 19:2).

They were good people. They had been baptized with John's baptism, a baptism of repentance. They had turned from sin. But they had stopped halfway. Paul baptized them in the name of the Lord Jesus, laid his hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came upon them. A little Pentecost in Ephesus.

Now, if Paul walked into our church this morning and asked the same question, what would we say? We would say: yes, of course, we were baptized and confirmed. But do we live like people who have received the Spirit? Do we ever pray to him? Do we ask his help before a hard decision? For many Christians, the Holy Spirit is the forgotten Person of the Trinity.

We are in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. This is the best time to get to know him. Pray every day: Come, Holy Spirit. Ask him for his gifts: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord. He is not an idea; he is a Person, and he is waiting to be asked.

In the Gospel Jesus knows that his disciples will run away that very night. Yet he says: take courage; I have conquered the world (John 16:33). The Spirit is the one who gives us that courage. The same frightened disciples, after Pentecost, would stand before rulers and say: we cannot keep from speaking.

Today we remember St John of Avila, a Spanish priest who was falsely accused and put in prison. In prison he did not grow bitter; he grew in love for Christ. He came out and became one of the great preachers of his time. That is what the Holy Spirit does. So let us ask him today: Come, Holy Spirit, and give us courage. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul met some people who had never heard of the Holy Spirit! He prayed with them, and the Holy Spirit came into their hearts.
You received the Holy Spirit when you were baptized. He is your best helper. When you are scared or need to be good, just say: Holy Spirit, help me!

intro: Theme: “Take courage; I have conquered the world!”
Disciples who had not heard of the Holy Spirit, the laying on of hands, and the courage that comes from Christ's victory.

sub: The forgotten Person of the Trinity.

He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” They replied, “No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
points.apply: Pray each day this week the prayer “Come, Holy Spirit,” and speak to him as a Person, not an idea.

points.h: Paul laid his hands on them
sub: Baptism in the name of Jesus.

points.apply: Thank God for your Confirmation, and pray this week for one young person preparing for it.

q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!
points.apply: Face one fear or difficulty this week in the name of Jesus, asking the Spirit for the gift of fortitude.

concl: Like the disciples at Ephesus, we need more than a beginning; we need the Holy Spirit, given in Baptism and Confirmation and renewed in prayer.
Christ has already conquered the world; in him we have peace, and through his Spirit, the courage of St John of Avila and of all the saints.
2027-05-10.resolve: Ask the Holy Spirit each day until Pentecost for one of his seven gifts.
